title: Quick Parisienne Gnocchi in Chive Butter
summary: Designed for busy weeknights, this French Parisienne gnocchi offers effortless bistro-style elegance in thirty-five minutes. Built around light choux pastry dumplings poached briefly in salted water, this version skips potato mashing entirely. The poached dumplings are pan-seared in rich brown butter with fresh chives, garlic, and Dijon mustard until light and crispy on the outside. Warm, pillowy centers contrast delightfully with golden pan-fried surfaces. This weeknight meal delivers classic French panache using standard pantry ingredients. High in protein from eggs and Gruyère cheese, it satisfies hunger while maintaining a refined profile. Piping choux dough directly into simmering water makes preparation remarkably quick and mess-free. Finish with freshly grated Parmesan and lemon zest for a bright, aromatic dish that feels like dining at a cozy Parisian bistro.

steps.step: Combine water, half of unsalted butter, and sea salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Bring water butter mixture to a rapid boil, ensuring butter melts completely into liquid.
Remove pot from heat source and add all-purpose flour all at once into hot liquid.
Stir mixture vigorously using a wooden spoon until flour absorbs water and forms ball.
Return pot to medium heat and cook dough for two minutes while stirring to dry out paste.
Transfer hot dough paste into a cool glass mixing bowl and spread slightly to cool down.
Allow dough paste to cool for four minutes so added eggs do not scramble prematurely.
Add Dijon mustard, ground nutmeg, and ground white pepper into cooled dough paste.
Add first egg to dough and beat vigorously with wooden spoon until fully incorporated.
Add second egg, beating thoroughly until dough paste turns smooth and glossy in bowl.
Add third egg and continue beating until dough reaches soft shiny dropping consistency.
Fold shredded Gruyere cheese and half of grated Parmesan cheese into choux paste.
Spoon finished choux dough paste into a heavy pastry piping bag fitted with half-inch round tip.
Set filled piping bag aside on counter while bringing poaching water pot to a gentle simmer.
Fill a wide shallow stockpot with four quarts of water and add one tablespoon sea salt.
Heat water until it reaches a gentle simmer with small bubbles breaking surface slowly.
Hold piping bag over simmering pot and squeeze out three-quarter inch lengths of dough.
Cut dough lengths cleanly using small sharp paring knife so dumplings drop into water.
Poach gnocchi dumplings in batches of twenty to avoid overcrowding simmering pot.
Cook gnocchi for three minutes after they float to surface to ensure dough cooks inside.
Remove floating poached dumplings gently using a slotted spider spoon from hot water.
Transfer dumplings onto a parchment-lined baking sheet greased lightly with olive oil.
Repeat piping and poaching process with remaining choux dough paste in piping bag.
Allow poached gnocchi to air-dry on parchment paper for five minutes before pan frying.
Finely mince shallot, garlic cloves, fresh chives, and fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves.
Zest one fresh lemon fine using a microplane, reserving lemon for fresh juice later.
Measure out remaining unsalted butter, white wine, heavy cream, and capers onto counter.
Check that poached gnocchi dumplings have cooled slightly and hold shape firmly.
Heat olive oil and one tablespoon butter in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
Place half of poached gnocchi into hot skillet in a single layer without crowding.
Sear gnocchi undisturbed for three minutes until bottom surfaces turn crisp and golden.
Shake pan and turn dumplings, searing second side for another two minutes until crisp.
Transfer golden gnocchi onto warm serving plate and sear remaining batch similarly.
Melt remaining butter in empty skillet over medium heat until foam subsides completely.
Add minced shallot and garlic, cooking for two minutes until soft and fragrant in pan.
Pour dry white wine into skillet, scraping bottom, and simmer for two minutes to reduce.
Stir in heavy cream, crème fraiche, capers, peas, and baby spinach into pan sauce.
Return all golden gnocchi to skillet, tossing gently to coat in warm chive butter sauce.
Stir in fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, red pepper flakes, and fresh minced chives.
Divide warm gnocchi and pan sauce evenly among four warm shallow pasta dishes.
Garnish top of each bowl with remaining Parmesan cheese, black pepper, and parsley.
Serve immediately while gnocchi dumplings remain crispy on outside and soft inside.
